abstract: This work presents a new methodology for video quality assessment using objective parameters based on image segmentation. The method is applied to a set of natural scenes and MPEG-2 video codecs. An image segmentation algorithm divides the scenes into three regions: plane, edges, and texture; and assigns a set of objective parameters to each region. A perceptual-based model is defined by computing the relationship between objective measures and results of subjective assessment tests. Thereafter, the model allows subjective rating prediction without human input. The work shows that region-based objective measurements provide more accurate predictions as compared to global measurements.

authors.affiliation: CPqD Research & Development Center, Campinas, Brazil
authors.bio: Antonio Claudio Franca Pessoa received a B.S. degree from the Federal University of Paraiba, Brazil, in 1985, and an M.S. degree from the State University of Campinas, Brazil, in 1990, both in electrical engineering. Since 1987, Pessoa has been at CPqD (Research and Development Center), where he has performed research in video and audio coding, video quality evaluation, and channel coding. His main interests include TV/HDTV digital transmission, voice recognition, and synthesis.

authors.bio: Alexandre Xavier Falcão received a B.S. in electrical engineering in 1988 from the Federal University of Pernambuco, Brazil. He has worked in image processing since 1991. In 1993, he received an M.S. in electrical engineering from the State University of Campinas, Brazil. — During 1994-1996, Falcão worked on user-steered image segmentation methods for his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania, EUA. In 1996, he received his Ph.D. in electrical engineering from the State University of Campinas, Brazil. — Falcão worked on video quality assessment methods at CPqD-Telebras in 1997 and 1998. Currently, he is an assistant professor at the State University of Campinas. His principal interests are in the areas of image processing and analysis, digital video, and medical imaging.
authors.name: A. Falcão

authors.affiliation: CPqD Research & Development Center, Campinas, Brazil
authors.bio: Ricardo Massahiro Nishihara received B.E.E. and M.S. degrees from the State University of Campinas, Brazil, in 1992 and 1995, respectively. Since 1994 he has been employed by CPqD (Research and Development Center), where he is a member of the Digital Signal Processing Division. His technical experience has been in areas of digital image processing, video coding, image quality assessment, digital television, and digital signal processing.
authors.name: R. Nishihara

authors.bio: Ana Eliza Faria e Silva graduated from the State University of Campinas, Brazil, where she received an M.S. degree in subjective evaluation of digital compressed images, in 1997. After graduating, she joined the Digital Signal Processing Division at the CPqD (Research and Development Center), where she worked for two years. She has been working at the Globo TV Network since 1998. Her current interests are the evaluation of new broadcast systems and high-definition television.
authors.name: A. Silva

authors.bio: Roberto Alencar Lotufo received an electronic engineering diploma from Instituto Tecnológico de Aeron´utica, Brazil, in 1978; an M.S. degree from the State University of Campinas, Brazil, in 1981; and a Ph.D. degree from the University of Bristol, U.K., in 1990, all in electrical engineering. — Since 1981, Lotufo has been with the Department of Computer Engineering and Industrial Automation at the State University of Campinas. His principal interests are in the areas of image processing applications, multidimensional image processing and analysis, mathematical morphology, video processing, and medical imaging.
